facts.value: Financial Performance 2025/26 - Unaudited Outturn, reported to Aberdeenshire Council on 25 June 2026 (doc 44919). General Fund and HRA revenue outturn plus General Services and HRA Capital Plan outturn against a 31 March 2026 year end. Report prepared by Karlyn Watt, Strategic Finance Manager; Director of Business Services Rob Simpson.

source.title: Financial Performance 2025/26 - Unaudited Outturn, Aberdeenshire Council, 25 June 2026

facts.note: This is a revenue/capital outturn report, NOT a treasury management report. It carries no CFR, no external borrowing total, no other long-term liabilities figure, no investment balance, no maturity profile, no weighted rate, no MRP policy statement, and no liability benchmark. The whole document is 21 pages of General Fund service variances, reserve movements and capital scheme slippage.

facts.value: Net under-budget position of £7.776m before transfers to reserves against a revised revenue budget of £830.238m (variance of less than 1%). After £7.708m of proposed reserve transfers and earmarking the net position reduces to £0.068m. Original budget was £821.596m. Q1 forecast was £8.476m over-budget, moving through £3.418m (Q2) and £0.765m (Q3) to the final under-budget position.
facts.note: Not a treasury figure. Included to record the paper's headline number.

facts.value: Capital Financing Costs (GF) budget £46.338m, actual £40.263m — £6.075m under budget (movement of £1.6m vs Q3 forecast). Attributed to 'ability to defer external borrowing as a result of lower capital expenditure and higher cash balances during the year'. Paper states 'New borrowing will require to be secured in early 2026/27 to maintain liquidity and support the timing of forecast cash flows.'
facts.note: The only treasury-adjacent commentary in the report. No amount given for the deferred borrowing, no resulting external debt figure, no CFR, no forward borrowing intention beyond the general 'early 2026/27' statement.

facts.value: HRA Total Net Income £9.111m against a revised budget of £7.308m — £1.803m better than budget. HRA Financing Costs budget £17.266m, actual £16.401m — £0.865m under budget, attributed at §5.2 to 'delayed borrowing arising from lower capital plan spend than budgeted' with 'higher cash balances have also generated additional interest during the year'.
facts.note: Same picture on the HRA as on the General Fund — deferred borrowing running the outturn favourably. No HRA CFR, no HRA-specific loan-book split, no HRA maturity view.

facts.value: General Services Capital Plan actual expenditure £65.485m against a revised budget of £96.127m — £30.642m below budget, 31.8% lower than planned. HRA Capital Plan actual expenditure £21.558m against revised budget of £31.413m — £9.855m below, 31.5% lower. Both variances attributed principally to slippage and rephasing (Peterhead Cultural Quarter, 1140 Hours, New Schools, Macduff Marine Aquarium, HIP2 tender delays, sheltered housing paused for review) rather than reductions in scope.
facts.note: The mechanism behind the deferred borrowing: capital spend came in £40m below plan across GF and HRA combined, so the borrowing that would have funded it did not need to be drawn. The rephasing into 2026/27 is what will drive the 'early 2026/27' borrowing mentioned at 4.23.

facts.value: Total reserves 1 April 2025 (£98.688m) → 31 March 2026 (£107.470m). Movements: Statutory Funds (£1.868m) → (£2.368m); Capital Earmarked (£11.772m) → (£12.926m); Risk and Inflation Reserve (£15.658m) → (£16.928m); Underwrite IJB Shortfall (£7.377m) → (£2.000m); Transformation Reserve (£21.343m) → (£25.348m); Transformation Payback Reserve 0 → (£1.419m); GF Earmarked (£19.005m) → (£22.717m); HRA Earmarked (£10.665m) → (£12.764m). Working Balances unchanged at (£11.000m) split £9.000m GF / £2.000m HRA. Reserves Strategy targets uncommitted GF balances of about 3.5% of net revenue budget, circa £29m.
facts.note: Reserves are moving up, not down — IJB underwriting reserve released £5.377m (£7.377m → £2m), with £4.005m proposed to Transformation and £4.458m added to Risk and Inflation. Nothing here is a treasury indicator.

facts.value: Total provisions 1 April 2025 £29.958m → 31 March 2026 £38.170m. Bad debt provisions rose from £22.552m to £26.049m; other provisions from £7.406m to £12.121m. Council Tax bad debt provision rose from £17.128m to £19.755m following a revised methodology introduced after external audit comments on optimism of previous assumptions. Sundry Debtor provision rose from £3.029m to £4.087m with £1.628m of write-offs. Asset Decommissioning provision rose from £6.656m to £9.514m, £1.878m from Aberdeenshire's share of the Energy from Waste plant decommissioning estimate (Aberdeen City lead authority) plus £1.734m for waste transfer sites, quarries and landfill sites.
facts.note: Recorded for completeness; not treasury but shows the wider prudence agenda picked up in the outturn.

facts.value: PWLBtoday holding for ABERDEENSHIRE COUNCIL at 31 March 2026: 143 PWLB loans, principal £949,786,945, weighted rate 3.5330%. Profile mix 50 ANNUITY / 76 MATURITY / 17 EIP. Live at 16 August 2026: 138 loans. Maturity today: 9 loans £30.021m under 12 months at 3.605%; 8 loans £30.144m in 1-2 years at 4.300%; 27 loans £80.408m in 2-5 years at 3.620%; 45 loans £292.854m in 5-10 years at 4.607%; 3 loans £20.001m in 10-25 years at 4.780%; 46 loans £484.350m at 25 years and over at weighted 2.763%.

source.title: PWLBtoday per-council PWLB loan file via price_book.py

facts.note: The £484m at 2.763% at 25 years and over is one of the biggest chunks of very-low-rate long-dated PWLB in the book — mostly the pre-2010 borrowing that Aberdeenshire has never had reason to refinance. The paper publishes no PWLB-specific figure, no total external borrowing, no maturity view and no weighted rate, so this cannot be tied against any printed line in the outturn report.

facts.value: Live 138 loans, balance £934,058,609. DMO premature repayment curve notice 314/26 PM as at 14 August 2026: indicative settlement £723,938,387, net DISCOUNT £210,120,222 (22.5% of principal). 62 loans below par, 75 above. Largest single discounts all on very long-dated low-coupon MATURITY loans: 376388 (MATURITY 2071-07-19, 1.72%, £25.0m) −£15,521,654; 376386 (MATURITY 2071-01-19, 1.73%, £25.0m) −£15,458,117; 450463 (MATURITY 2055-12-08, 1.62%, £25.0m) −£14,164,754; 176065 (MATURITY 2068-03-26, 1.29%, £20.0m) −£13,664,748.

source.title: PWLBtoday canonical break-cost engine, DMO notice 314/26 PM

Recorded for completeness; not raised in any email because the paper says nothing about the loan book to hook off, and a first-contact email about a £210m discount would be advice about a decision only replacement-cost analysis (which we do not model) could actually resolve.

facts.value: LOAN-BOOK RECONCILIATION: NOT POSSIBLE. The paper does not print a PWLB count, total borrowing figure, weighted rate or any per-loan detail. Our file at year-end shows 143 loans / £949,786,945 / 3.5330% weighted for ABERDEENSHIRE COUNCIL, but there is no line in the paper to tie against. BALANCE-SHEET IDENTITY (CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing): NOT POSSIBLE. None of CFR, external borrowing or other long-term liabilities is printed anywhere in the document — the paper is a revenue/capital outturn and does not carry balance-sheet treasury figures. TABLE ARITHMETIC (verified): Table 1 General Fund reconciles to Net Expenditure (£27.660m) against Revised Budget (£19.884m) giving a £7.776m under-budget position; the £7.708m transfer-to-reserves line reduces this to £0.068m as the paper narrates (p4). Table 2 HRA reconciles Total Expenditure £67.720m and Income (£76.831m) to Net Income £9.111m; CFCR £9.136m plus £0.025m reserve movement balances the account (p11). Table 4 Reserves opening £98.688m + net movement £8.782m ≈ closing £107.470m (p13). Table 6 Capital Directorate lines sum to £65.485m against revised £96.127m variance £30.642m (p15). Table 8 Provisions opening £29.958m − £1.628m write-offs + £9.840m increases = £38.170m closing (p17). All internal to the paper — no external cross-check available.

source.title: Financial Performance 2025/26 Tables 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and PWLBtoday price_book.py

facts.note: The paper's own tables reconcile cleanly. What CANNOT be verified is anything treasury-side: no CFR, no external debt total, no OLTL, no PWLB share, no maturity view, no rate. This is because it is a revenue outturn report, not a treasury outturn — those figures live in Aberdeenshire's separate annual treasury management outturn report which we do not hold.

facts.value: Not to be raised in an email: (a) the £210m indicative break-cost discount on our live loan-book pricing — 22.5% of principal, with four single loans over £13m below par — is a striking headline but a first contact framed around it would be advice about a treasury decision that only the council's replacement-cost analysis (which we do not model) can settle, and the paper carries no discussion of the loan book to hook off; (b) the £484m of PWLB at 25+ years at a weighted 2.763% is likely the largest low-coupon long-dated PWLB position in our library, but again the paper does not discuss it; (c) the paper's Table 1 does not print a Net Expenditure row-heading — it's just implied by the negative signs on the components — a minor disclosure quirk; (d) '£7,708m' vs '£7.708m' formatting appears in §4.37 vs Table 1 (thousands vs millions with the same delimiter); (e) the paper's own text at §4.37 says the total transfer 'is in excess of the revised budget by £7.708m' but the Table 1 'Usable Reserves - In Year Movement' row shows £27.592m actual vs £19.884m revised (£7.708m excess) — the paper and table tie, so this is only noted; (f) Karlyn Watt (Strategic Finance Manager) is the report preparer and Rob Simpson (Director of Business Services) the signatory — neither is the S151, whose name and email are not printed anywhere; (g) the report does not name a next treasury cycle date — Aberdeenshire's annual treasury outturn is a separate paper likely due September/October to Audit Committee, and this report does not cross-refer to it.

summary.text:
This is Aberdeenshire's revenue and capital outturn report for 2025/26, not a treasury management report. It carries no CFR, no external borrowing total, no other long-term liabilities figure, no PWLB share, no maturity profile, no weighted rate, no MRP policy statement and no liability benchmark. The only treasury-adjacent content in the whole 21-page document is a single sentence at §4.23 explaining that Capital Financing Charges came in £6.075m under budget (£40.263m vs £46.338m budget) because external borrowing was deferred, plus a matching HRA sentence at §5.2 explaining the £0.865m HRA financing under-budget the same way. Neither carries the deferred amount, the resulting external debt total, or the CFR. The paper does state that 'new borrowing will require to be secured in early 2026/27 to maintain liquidity and support the timing of forecast cash flows'.

Loan-book reconciliation is therefore not possible: our file holds 143 PWLB loans for ABERDEENSHIRE COUNCIL at 31 March 2026 for £949,786,945 principal at a weighted 3.5330% — a very large book, weighted with £484m of 25+ year PWLB at 2.763% — but the paper prints no PWLB figure to tie this against. The balance-sheet identity CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing is not possible either because none of the three inputs is published in this report. What the paper's own tables do carry (Table 1 General Fund, Table 2 HRA, Table 4 Reserves, Tables 6/7 Capital, Table 8 Provisions) all reconcile cleanly internally.

No email is drafted. The report has no reconcilable treasury figure to open with, no printed maturity or benchmark line to work off, no LOBO exposure to observe, no MRP change to note, and no dated forecast to test against today's curve. The four things this template asks for as first-contact material — a loan-book tie-back, a printed indicator moving, a dated assumption to test, or a pattern only visible across the library — none of them can be sourced from this paper. Aberdeenshire's annual treasury management outturn report is a separate document and would be the natural venue for that reading; when the reading library catches it, a proper draft becomes possible.

No officer address is published in this paper. Karlyn Watt (Strategic Finance Manager) is the report preparer and Rob Simpson (Director of Business Services) is the signatory; neither is the S151, whose name and email do not appear anywhere in the document.
